final_method_items.summary: Main function of this pass. Find and propagate all three types of copy statements (see pass description above). This is an implementation of an algorithm from the paper Simple and Efficient Construction of Static Single Assignmemnt Form[1]. It is based on strongly-connected components (SCCs) in dataflow graph. The original algorithm only considers PHI statements. We extend it to also consider assignment statements of type _2 = _1;. The algorithm is based on this definition of a set of redundant PHIs[1]: A non-empty set P of PHI functions is redundant iff the PHI functions just reference each other or one other value It uses this lemma[1]: Let P be a redundant set of PHI functions. Then there is a strongly-connected component S subset of P that is also redundant. The algorithm works in this way: 1 Find SCCs 2 For each SCC S in topological order: 3 Construct set 'inner' of statements that only have other statements from S on their right hand side 4 Construct set 'outer' of values that originate outside S and appear on right hand side of some statement from S 5 If |outer| = 1, outer only contains a value v. Statements in S only refer to each other or to v -- they are redundant. Propag

behavior_items: The program defines two nested aggregate types: `struct a` contains five scalar fields (`int b`, `int c`, `short d`, `int e`, `int f`), and `struct g` contains two `struct a` members named `f` and `h`. The global `int i` is zero-initialized by default because it has static storage duration.

In `main`, local variable `l` is initialized with ten scalar constants that fill both embedded `struct a` objects in declaration order. Thus `l.f` becomes `{2, 1, 6, 1, 1}` and `l.h` becomes `{7, 5, 1, 0, 1}`. In particular, the tested field `l.h.b` is a compile-time constant `7`, which is nonzero.

The loop `for (; i; ++i) bar31_();` executes only while global `i` is nonzero. Since `i` starts at zero unless changed before entry by the environment, the loop is unreachable on normal entry to `main`. Even if the compiler keeps the loop, the loop body and increment do not modify any local aggregates `j`, `l`, `m`, or `k`, so they cannot affect the later value copied from `l.h.b`.

After the loop, the code performs a pure chain of whole-struct copies: `j = l; struct g m = j; struct g k = m;`. These are value-preserving copies of the same object state. Therefore `k` is exactly equal to `l`, and `k.h.b` must still be `7`.

The conditional `if (k.h.b) ; else foo();` therefore has a statically known condition. Because `k.h.b` is provably nonzero, control always takes the empty then-branch and the `else` arm containing `foo()` is dead code. A sufficiently optimized compiler should fold the condition to true and eliminate the call entirely.

GCC 12.2 at `-Os` performs that reasoning successfully. Its output removes all aggregate materialization and all struct-copy code, and it also eliminates the `foo` call. The generated assembly only checks whether `i` is zero to decide whether the loop is skipped or executed, then returns directly.

The newer trunk compiler shown in the report regresses: it still emits stack space for aggregate temporaries, copies the constant object `l` into one stack slot, later copies that slot into another stack slot, then loads the field at offset `20(%rsp)` corresponding to `k.h.b`, compares it with zero, and conditionally calls `foo`. This means the optimizer failed to propagate the known constant value through the copy chain strongly enough for dead-code elimination.

The emitted trunk assembly demonstrates the exact exercised behavior: `.LC0` holds the ten initializer words for `l`; `rep movsl` first copies that constant block to stack storage for one local aggregate and later copies it again to another stack region; `cmpl $0, 20(%rsp)` tests the `b` field of the second embedded `struct a` inside the final copied object; and because GCC no longer recognizes that value as constant nonzero, the dead `foo` edge remains.

The reproducer is therefore stressing inter-pass interaction among aggregate copy lowering, constant propagation, value numbering, and dead code elimination under `-Os`. The bug is not about runtime correctness of the source program itself, but about the compiler losing the fact that a field read after several aggregate copies still has a known constant value.

The regression is especially visible because the source contains no writes to any copied field after initialization, no aliasing through pointers, and no calls between the copies that could legally clobber the locals. This makes `foo()` an ideal candidate for elimination and highlights that the missed optimization is due to compiler analysis degradation rather than ambiguous source semantics.

The bug report notes a bisect to commit `f6c168f8c06047...`, so the reproducer is intended to isolate a change after GCC 12 that inhibits dead code elimination when a constant aggregate is copied through multiple local temporaries and then one field is tested.

Semantically, the whole function is equivalent to: run the `bar31_` loop while `i != 0`, then return 0. The aggregate declarations, assignments, and the `foo` branch are observationally redundant because the tested field is a compile-time true constant. GCC 12 reaches that reduced form; the regressed trunk build does not.
